records.title: Is “Consciousness” a Folk Psychological Concept?
records.author: Victor Machado Barcellos
records.observation: In vignette studies reviewed by Barcellos, respondents judged whether a human or robot saw red or felt pain. These were judgements about agents, not measurements of the agents’ experiences.
records.interpretation: Barcellos argues that phenomenal consciousness is a specialist concept rather than a concept shared in ordinary thinking.
records.alternative: Seeing red can mean detecting a colour. Vignette wording and conversational context can affect attribution without establishing that respondents lack the concept.
records.prism: Record the exact question, population and response measure. Identify the respondent separately from the agent being judged.
records.omni: Separate detection, attributed experience and first-person experience.
records.akashicnet: Describe the finding as a difference in attributions; leave the robot’s experience undetermined.

records.title: Revisiting the Neural Correlates of Consciousness
records.author: Francis T. Fallon and Michael Pitts
records.observation: The essay describes an imagined EEG task with multiple signals separated in time. It reports no observations from that task.
records.interpretation: The authors propose that several processes unfolding over time may contribute to conscious experience.
records.alternative: A signal might reflect priming, memory retrieval or report preparation rather than the onset of perception.
records.prism: Mark hypothetical inputs as illustrative. For empirical work, retain stimulus, measurement and report times separately.
records.omni: Distinguish perception, access, memory and report. Treat timing as a question rather than a fixed stage.
records.akashicnet: Label the proposal as a perspective, not a finding that consciousness is discontinuous.

records.title: From Cacophony to Hierarchy
records.author: Shamil Chandaria and colleagues
records.observation: The report compares candidate indicators at behavioural, computational, causal, organismic and organism–environment levels. Its numerical examples use stipulated inputs.
records.interpretation: The authors propose weighing indicator evidence alongside confidence in the theories that make the indicators relevant.
records.alternative: A different theory, indicator coding or prior can substantially change the model output.
records.prism: Retain observed indicators and assumed inputs in distinct fields. Mark illustrative numbers as model outputs.
records.omni: Tag the level of description. A claim about one level does not automatically support a claim about another.
records.akashicnet: Present the outputs as sensitivity examples, not measured probabilities of consciousness.

records.title: What Can Analogy Tell Us About Artificial Consciousness?
records.author: Keith J. Holyoak and Martin M. Monti
records.observation: The essay draws on anaesthesia, neurological conditions and comparative research to discuss the relationship between mechanisms and observable behaviour.
records.interpretation: The authors argue that resemblance in causally relevant mechanisms carries more weight than outward similarity alone.
records.alternative: Different mechanisms might support experience; a weak analogy to humans does not exclude that possibility.
records.prism: Label analogies as inferences and name the source and target of each comparison.
records.omni: State the proposed mechanism, why it matters and which alternative mechanisms remain open.
records.akashicnet: Avoid treating fluent behaviour as proof, or weak analogy as proof of impossibility.

records.title: How Seriously Should We Take AI Welfare?
records.author: Preston Lennon
records.kind: philosophical argument about knowledge and welfare
records.observation: The article reviews scientific theories of consciousness. It does not report an experiment measuring AI experience.
records.interpretation: Lennon argues that uncertainty about the available theories should constrain how seriously we take AI welfare in action and policy.
records.alternative: Precaution might still be justified under substantial uncertainty, depending on the costs and consequences of acting or waiting.
records.prism: Distinguish claims about evidence, confidence and policy in the source record.
records.omni: Separate confidence in a theory from confidence that a particular system satisfies it.
records.akashicnet: Record the judgement about consciousness separately from any reasons to act.
